technical_summary: After 10-week Hosted API trial: steady-state ~6 QPS (avg concurrency 3), peak bursts up to 28 QPS (~20 concurrent), token mix ~60% embeddings (avg 128 tokens per request), 30% chat/generation (avg prompt 45 tokens / completion 220 tokens), 10% reranking. Latency SLO target 250ms p95 for chat; embeddings less latency-sensitive but throughput-bound. Baseline Dedicated recommendation: 4-GPU pool with autoscale to +2 GPUs for bursts, KV prefix caching for repeated prompts, batching for embeddings. Expect ~1.2B tokens/month at current runway; cost sensitivity high — looking to reduce per-token unit cost by ~35% vs hosted pay-as-you-go.
notes:
CRM notes — rough, from AE/SE/PM sync:
- OakBound = mid-market product analytics SaaS, multi-tenant product, strong PLG motion.
- Use cases prioritized: fast in-app support agent (context windows ~4k tokens), doc-search/semantic ranking across product docs (embedding-heavy), and occasional long-form summarization for release notes.
- POC highlights: hosted trial integrated via SDK in 3 days; indexed 1.2M docs -> heavy embedding ingestion overnight. Team saw 2x improvement in semantic search relevance vs existing vector DB pipeline.
- Quote from CTO on 2026-01-19 call: "We need predictable unit economics — bursts kill our budget. If Dedicated gets us 30% cheaper with same latency, we're in."
- SE notes: embedding workload dominates token volume; suggest dedicated batching cluster tuned for int8 quantized model for embeddings and separate low-latency chat cluster.
- Sizing detail captured during workshop: typical session = user query -> retrieve 12 chunks -> 12 embedding lookups (embedding model small) + 1 chat call for final answer. Average QPS profile by hour attached in Drive doc.
- Security: require SSO/SAML, KMS integration for customer secrets, audit logs retention 13 months, and VPC peering. Air-gapped not required.
- Procurement: procurement lead expects 60-day review for contracts >$200k ARR. Legal concerned about cross-region data residency (EU customers ~8% of users).
- Next steps (short): 1) Redwood to send Dedicated sizing worksheet and revised pricing (Carlos). 2) OakBound to share traffic forecast for next 12 months (rounded by feature). 3) Legal to start redline (Leah coordinating).
- Blockers: need final internal traffic forecast (we've asked product analytics for 95th percentile QPS by feature), Finance needs committed discount tiers to model ARR.
- Good win indicators: Redwood provides per-token committed pricing + clear fallback routing policy and autoscale SLA.
- Misc references: Jira INF-1298 for async batching bug during POC; SEC-4421 for KMS questions.
